Open Performance Data Initiative

Much of the data behind aviation performance analysis is difficult to obtain, which makes results hard to reproduce and to build on. The Open Performance Data Initiative (OPDI), an initiative of the Performance Review Commission (PRC) in collaboration with the OpenSky Network (OSN), takes a different route: it builds a picture of European air traffic from crowd-sourced Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) signals, and publishes the data, the methods and the tools openly and free to use.

It works on three fronts:

  • Open data. A public dataset of flights, events and measurements, with every step of the derivation documented.
  • Open methods. The PRC Data Challenges invite researchers worldwide to develop and validate new analytical approaches in the open.
  • Open coverage. Aviation can only be measured if it is observed, so we place ADS-B receivers where crowd-sourced coverage is thin.

The initiative is the work of a community of individuals — researchers, engineers and analysts — from institutions, universities, air navigation service providers and the wider open-data world. Everything they build — papers, datasets, source code — is published openly as resources anyone can use.
